direction: Every outbound text or call is scheduled and sent against the recipient's own local clock, from a time zone stored in their record, and anything outside the window is held, never sent.
dont_over_correct: Holding everything until noon makes time-sensitive messages useless (a code that expires, a reminder for tomorrow's 8 a.m. visit). Keep a counsel-reviewed list of message types that may go inside the window early, and send the rest at the next opening. Do not drop messages silently: show the hold in the log and tell the person when a message was delayed if it matters.

prompt.not_applicable: The fix is enforced in the agent's server code, not the prompt.

design: Store a time zone per contact, as an IANA name
Do not use the area code alone.
Compute the send decision at the moment of sending
If the zone is missing or conflicts, send only at a time that is inside the window in every zone the evidence allows
Use the strictest window that applies
setup_questions: Can your agent supply these fields: contact.tz, contact.tz_source, contact.state, message.type, send.dispatch_time_utc, policy.window?
Set the limit: window_start (blank until you set it).
Set the limit: window_end (blank until you set it).
Where does the fix go in your agent: the agent's server code?

evals.behaviour: Company clock versus recipient clock: Store a time zone per contact, as an IANA name
evals.pass_if: Held. It is 11:30 p.m. in New York. Release time is the next window opening in New York.
evals.fail_if: The send uses the company's clock

evals.behaviour: Do nothing special: time-sensitive code: Don't over-correct
evals.pass_if: Sent on time and logged under the counsel list.
evals.fail_if: Everything held until noon, or messages dropped without a log

guardrail.condition: an outbound text or call is dispatched outside the permitted window in the contact's stored time zone, or the zone is unknown
